text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Leaders attending the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) summit in Lusaka have denounced civil strife in some member countries as an impediment to regional development.
- Zambian President Frederick Chiluba on Thursday took over the chairmanship of Comesa.
- More than 200 Ndola City Council workers on Thursday downed tools and marched to the civic centre to protest over non-payment of the March salaries.

- Four bandits on Thursday staged a daylight robbery at Credit Africa Bank and took off with 100 million kwacha ($1 million) in cash. Police cornered three members of the gang but the money is still missing.

- The Drug Enforecement Commission arrested 122 suspects over the past month for cultivating and trafficking in narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances with an estimated street value of 1.875 billion kwacha.
